acceptance: The ADR records the seven owner decisions in the context of this item, replaces decisions 1 and 6 and the consequences that rule out custom Rust code, and keeps the budgets, provenance and validation gates that still apply.

The ADR defines the library's crate layout, the PyO3/Arrow C Data Interface boundary, the determinism model (fixed-block per-table RNG, cross-thread and cross-platform bit-exactness), wheel platforms, and per-generator budgets and gates for the cutover.
The ADR states what happens to the parked items (tpcgen-cli adapter, Python vectorisation, SSB migration, cutovers, trailing-delimiter adoption) and to the existing streaming converter.

Tracker items exist for building the library in stages (repository and crate skeleton, TPC-H, TPC-DS, SSB, synthetic generators, Parquet writer, BenchBox integration, cutovers, legacy retirement decision), each with needs, decision gates and verification rubrics; superseded items are dropped with a reason.
The ADR revision merges by PR after owner approval of the revised text.
context:
Owner decisions (2026-11-25, dialog): the goal of the datagen effort is a new BenchBox-owned Rust data generation library, with the cutover to it only after it passes the gates.
1. Scope: TPC-H, TPC-DS, SSB and the synthetic generators in one library, staged TPC first, then SSB and the synthetic generators.
2. TPC base: depend on the upstream Apache-2.0 tpcgen-rs crates (tpchgen, tpcdsgen) as library dependencies; send fixes upstream; no fork.
3. Binding: PyO3 extension module with abi3 wheels, streaming Arrow record batches through the Arrow C Data Interface.
4. Parquet: written directly in Rust with BenchBox types and the row-group policy; delimited output stays available for loaders that need it.
5. Compatibility: TPC delimited output byte-identical to dbgen/dsdgen after trailing-delimiter stripping; synthetic and SSB output may change under a per-benchmark version bump with golden hashes.
6. Home: new repository BenchBox-dev/benchbox-datagen, an optional dependency until it passes the gates, then the default, with the bundled C binaries kept as a fallback until a retirement decision.
7. In flight: finish datagen-p1-deterministic-parquet-writer; do not ship the tpcgen-cli adapter as an interim backend; park the Python vectorisation and the cutover items until the revised ADR is accepted.

Owner decisions on draft points (2026-11-25, dialog): (1) at the first cutover benchbox-datagen becomes a required dependency on every platform with a wheel; platforms without one resolve to legacy from a fixed platform table and say so; no auto mode, no silent fallback. (2) TPC-DS SF < 1 and the TPC-H RF1/RF2 and TPC-DS -update refresh sets are implemented byte-identically in the library (or upstream) before any TPC cutover. (3) Repository licence MIT. (4) The draft's tighter per-benchmark budgets are the gate: tpch and tpcds SF>=1 <=3 s delimited / <=4 s Parquet at SF 1 and <=30/<=40 s at SF 10; ssb, h2odb, tsbs_devops, clickbench, vector_search, coffeeshop <=5/<=6 s and <=50/<=60 s, <=512/<=1,024 MiB; tpch_skew, amplab, joinorder_synthetic <=8/<=10 s and <=80/<=100 s, <=512/<=1,024 MiB.
description: docs/internal/adr/adr-benchbox-datagen.md (accepted in #4483) adopts the upstream tpcgen-cli wheel through a subprocess adapter, rewrites synthetic generators in Python/NumPy, and builds a Rust repository only on a measured budget miss. The owner's intent is a new Rust data generation library and a cutover to it. Revise the ADR to record that target and its design, then rebuild the phase 2 and phase 3 tracker items around it.
